symptom: Applying the vacation accessibility filter showed 0 places and an empty state even though the supplier-derived catalog contains accessible places.
expected_behavior: Every vacation place carrying the verified accessible search identity appears in applied results and the filter-drawer preview, while unverified places remain excluded.
environment: Local release worktree fix/home-transient-state-20261103 on 2026-11-03, bundled 573-place vacation catalog, desktop 1440x1000 and mobile 390x844.

steps: Project the bundled vacation catalog through publicVacationSearchProperties.
Apply the former UI predicate hasVerifiedAccessibilityFeature to the compact three-feature cards.
reproduction.evidence: The diagnostic produced projectedAccessibleIds=4 and projectedVisibleExact=0, reproducing the screenshot's false empty result.

observations.observation: Four projected vacation entries retain the canonical accessible ID.
observations.evidence: vacation-1805, vacation-1977, vacation-1982 and vacation-2500 in the Node catalog diagnostic.

observations.observation: The public search projection intentionally keeps only the first three display features but preserves all search filter IDs.
The search page used the truncated display features for accessibility in two applied and two draft paths instead of the canonical matcher.

hypotheses.mechanism: The UI bypasses canonical searchFilterIds and re-evaluates a truncated display-feature list.
hypotheses.prediction: Canonical IDs remain nonzero while the UI feature predicate returns zero.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare projected searchFilterIds against hasVerifiedAccessibilityFeature on projected features.
hypotheses.result: 4 canonical accessible entries versus 0 matches from the former UI predicate.

hypotheses.mechanism: The supplier catalog contains no accessible vacation places.
hypotheses.prediction: No original or projected property carries the accessible identity.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Generate vacationSearchFilterIds for all bundled vacation places.
hypotheses.result: Four source and projected properties carry accessible, rejecting an empty supplier inventory.

hypotheses.mechanism: The URL parameter is not restored into filter state.
hypotheses.prediction: accessible=1 would not remain selected after load or reload.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Open and reload the local URL with accessible=1 on desktop and mobile.
hypotheses.result: The accessibility control remained pressed and the same four cards persisted on both viewports.

fix.change: Use matchesVacationSearchFilter for accessibility in both applied and draft filtering, allowing the preserved canonical ID to lead and source text to remain only a fallback.
fix.evidence: After the change, the focused suite passed 18 of 18 tests and local desktop, mobile and mobile draft checks all returned four verified places.

regression_checks.check: Compact accessibility identity survives display-feature truncation and excludes unverified properties.
Applied and draft UI paths use the canonical matcher.
Desktop and mobile accessible=1 render all four catalog matches and persist after reload.
Mobile draft preview displays 4 places and applies to the semantic results route.
regression_checks.evidence: verify-accessibility-filter.mjs output: mobile-draft label 'הצגת 4 מקומות', applied=true.

remaining_unknowns: The public environment still contains the old implementation until a separately authorized deployment occurs.
authorization_boundary: Local code repair, tests and commit only. No public deployment or supplier data mutation.
